_comment: Expected COMMAND-LAYER shadow-parity diffs, consumed by scripts/verify/command_parity_report.php (created 2026-07-27). Sibling of expected_diffs.json, which covers the ENGINE_MODE stream (reports/shadow/engine-*.jsonl); this file covers the COMMAND_LAYER stream (reports/shadow/command-*.jsonl). An entry matches a row when legacy_blocked/command_blocked equal the row's values, the cited rule_id is among the row's command_failures, and (if 'op' is present) the op matches. Every entry must cite an audit finding id. Scope is add+remove only: replace-component and transition-status are v2-only actions with no legacy counterpart.
_note_why_the_add_entries_mirror_expecte: AddComponentCommand evaluates the SAME ValidationEngine rule registry that ServerBuilder's ENGINE_MODE hook does, so every audit-approved engine-vs-legacy divergence reappears in the command stream. The six add-side entries below are therefore the same six classes as expected_diffs.json's entries, restated with command_blocked instead of engine_blocked -- NOT independent approvals. If an entry is ever added to or removed from expected_diffs.json, mirror it here. Confirmed against real production rows: command-20260723.jsonl contains cpu.requires_board (legacy blocked, command allowed) and pcie.lane_budget (legacy allowed, command blocked) exactly as these entries describe.
_note_storage_bay_capacity_deliberately_: storage.bay_capacity is NOT an expected diff. The 2026-07-25 session found the rule was harsher than the legacy code that actually executes (ComponentValidator::validateChassisBayStorage():1024-1029 accepts a 2.5in drive in a 3.5in bay via a caddy and only warns) and corrected the rule to match. Any post-2026-07-25 bay_capacity divergence is a REGRESSION and must surface as unexplained -- do not add an entry to silence it.

entries._why: U-R.8 (audit R-1). Legacy ServerBuilder::removeComponent()'s ONLY dependency check is nic->sfp, so removing a motherboard or chassis silently strands the cpu/ram/cards that depend on it -- the defect the owner reported. DependencyBlockedRemovalRule blocks that removal instead, offering cascade=true. This divergence is the intended fix, not a defect: at COMMAND_LAYER_ENABLED=enforce a removal that legacy silently allowed now returns a dependency_blocked error with a cascade hint. Observed live in command-20260722.jsonl (chassis removal, cascade=false).
Mirrors expected_diffs.json's cpu.socket_count entry -- same rule, same audit finding, evaluated through AddComponentCommand instead of the ENGINE_MODE hook.

Mirrors expected_diffs.json's cpu.requires_board entry (the ERROR->VALIDATION_FAILURE relaxation, which by design does not block at ADD and re-blocks at finalize). Observed live in command-20260723.jsonl at 00:19:27.
Mirrors expected_diffs.json's pcie.lane_budget entry. Observed live in command-20260723.jsonl on hbacard, pciecard and storage adds.

Same ERROR->VALIDATION_FAILURE relaxation as cpu.requires_board: legacy hard-blocks a caddy-less drive at ADD, the engine defers the objection to VALIDATE/FINALIZE so a half-built draft can still be edited. Observed live 2026-07-28T15:28:31Z and 15:29:01Z. PREVIOUSLY EXEMPTED BY ASSUMPTION, NOT BY ENTRY: _note_storage_caddy_pairing in expected_diffs.json argued no entry was needed because the rule 'can never disagree with legacy's own never-blocks-at-add behavior'. That premise is simply false -- legacy's add path DOES block on a missing caddy, and these two production rows are the counterexample. The deferral is only sound because the objection genuinely re-blocks later, which was NOT true until F-26 (2026-07-29) made FINALIZE subsume VALIDATE; before that the rule blocked nowhere finalize reached. Confirmed re-blocking live at 2026-07-28T20:11:27Z.

_note_onboard_nic_fail_closed: Deliberately NOT an entries row -- same posture as expected_diffs.json's identically-named note. AddComponentCommand::apply()'s fail-closed onboard-NIC materialization throws CommandFailed('onboard_nic_failed'), which is not a rule verdict and emits no rule_id, so a fabricated matcher could never match it. In the command shadow stream it would appear as dry_run_failed rather than as a diff. Approved deliberate behavior change; see migration/handoffs/U-B.4-SIGNOFF-20260721.md.
_note_storage_caddy_pairing_rides_along: PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-07-29 by the storage.caddy_pairing entry above -- kept because the ride-along observation is still true and still useful. What remains correct: storage.caddy_pairing is VALIDATION_FAILURE, does not block at ADD, and therefore appears inside command_failures on rows whose diff was caused by some OTHER rule (e.g. pcie.lane_budget) without being the cause itself; those rows are still earned by the co-occurring blocking rule, not by this one. What was WRONG: the closing claim that it 'needs no entry of its own'. It does, for rows where legacy blocks the add and the command allows it -- observed twice in production on 2026-07-28. Riding along and being the cause are different cases and the file now covers both.
_note_legacy_unknown_rows: Every remove row written before 2026-07-27 carries no legacy_blocked at all -- the old inline writer logged from inside `if ($commandVerdict->blocking())`, i.e. BEFORE ServerBuilder::removeComponent() had run, so legacy's outcome was unknowable at write time and agreement was indistinguishable from divergence. command_parity_report.php counts those rows as legacy_unknown and excludes them from the comparison rather than guessing. They cannot be recovered retroactively; only post-fix traffic can.
_note_ram_type_incompatible_entry_retire: RETIRED 2026-07-29, same day it was added -- recorded rather than silently dropped. The entry excused a legacy-blocked/command-allowed finalize diff caused by SERVER_BUILD_GUIDE Bug 2 (ComponentValidator::validateRAMTypeCompatibility() compared memory types RAW, so 'DDR4' vs a board's 'DDR4 ECC' was false). Investigating it showed the bug was not incidental: ALL 7 available motherboard models declare memory.type 'DDR4 ECC' with no supported_types and NO ram in ims-data is typed 'DDR4 ECC', so legacy rejected EVERY finalize in the fleet and no configuration had ever reached status 3. Bug 2 was therefore FIXED in legacy (normalize both operands, reusing DataNormalizationUtils::normalizeMemoryType) instead of being permanently excused here. Both sides now agree; verified live 2026-07-28T21:15:32Z with a legacy-allowed/command-allowed finalize row -- the both-allow direction that had been structurally unreachable. Pre-fix rows are excluded by run_all.php's PARITY_SINCE_DEFAULT (2026-07-28T20:12), which is the documented mechanism for rows that predate a fix. Regression test: tests/unit/validation/ram_type_normalization_test.php.
